review.evidenceBasis: Title-only posture, tightened rule. 11 spec-level rejects: A-level-only formalisations carried by GCSE videos (flux definitions, binding energy, first law, I-V sketching, polarisation, I=Anvq, centre of gravity, hydrostatic derivation, equilibrium-with-torque) where the title does not name the clause.

rejects.reason: GCSE 'Gravitational Potential Energy' teaches ΔE=mgΔh; the gravitational-potential field concept of 13.4.3 is a distinct A-level framing, not title-evidenced.
GCSE 'Magnetic Fields' — the magnetic-flux definition of 20.5.1 is not title-evidenced.
Same video: flux-density definition (F=BIL formalisation, 20.2.3) not title-evidenced; a Doodle 'Motor Effect' medium binding already serves 20.2.3.
Binding energy per nucleon (23.1.6) is A-level-only, not title-evidenced in a GCSE fission/fusion video.
Polarisation (7.5.1) is an A-level-only clause, not title-evidenced in a GCSE transverse/longitudinal waves video.
'Resistance of a Filament Lamp' — the I–V characteristics sketching clause of 9.3.3 is a distinct skill, not title-evidenced.
GCSE 'Internal Energy' — the first law of thermodynamics ΔU=q+W (16.2.2) not title-evidenced.
GCSE 'Resultant Forces' — the equilibrium condition incl. zero resultant torque (4.2.2) not title-evidenced.
GCSE 'Atmospheric Pressure' — the hydrostatic Δp=ρgΔh derivation of 4.3.3 is a different frame, not title-evidenced.
'Gravity and Weight' — the centre-of-gravity clause of 4.1.1 not title-evidenced.
I=Anvq (9.1.4) is an A-level-only formula, not title-evidenced in a GCSE charge/current/voltage video.
